channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Mass protests sweep France as huge crowds demand higher wages
item.description: Hundreds of thousands of striking workers protested across France on Thursday, November 5, against the rising cost of living following weeks of youth-led demonstrations, with police firing tear gas as clashes broke out in some cities. FRANCE 24's Emily Boyle reports.

item.title: California governor says commuting all death sentences in state
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom said Thursday, November 5, he was commuting all death sentences across the state to life imprisonment, in a move that will affect over 500 prisoners. FRANCE 24's correspondent Wassim Cornet reports.

item.title: Netanyahu rival Eisenkot secures broad backing in bid to form government
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he will announce on Sunday, November 8, whom he will task with trying to form a new government, after the opposition's Gadi Eisenkot secured a commanding number of recommendations to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert has more.

item.title: 'Ramayana': Ancient Hindu epic and India's most expensive film
item.description: A big-budget film adaptation of the Ramayana, one of Hinduism's most revered epics, has renewed attention on the ancient tale that continues to shape India's culture, identity and politics. "Ramayana: Rise of a Legend", featuring Bollywood star Ranbir Kapoor, was released in India on Thursday, November 5, two days before the country's biggest festival of Diwali.

item.title: Fill in the blank in the quiz: Vance says they lost the midterms because of ____
item.description: Plus: Heidi Klum's hand, hackers and the pope's visitor!

item.title: Low birth rates were emptying public schools. ICE deportations are now making it worse
item.description: School enrollment was already expected to plunge by 2 million kids by 2030. Education experts say deporting immigrant families, many with school-age children, is making the crisis worse. (Image credit: Carlos Jaramillo for NPR)

item.title: 'Sleazy', 'manipulative' and 'ruthless': Russell Brand convicted of rape, sexual assault
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Friday, November 6: Italian, British, French and Bulgarian papers discuss the bomb threats that diverted multiple flights across Europe on Thursday. British papers discuss Russell Brand's rape and sexual assault conviction. Finally, kids in Hanoi chase tourists – not for money, but for vocabulary. Bonus: we learn a fun fact about chihuahuas.

item.title: Two 16 year olds charged after five boys seriously injured at Halloween party
item.description: Two 16 year olds have been charged after five boys were seriously injured at a party on Halloween.

item.title: Election 2026 live results: Karen Bass concedes LA mayoral race to Nithya Raman
item.description: Raman is poised to become the 44th mayor of the nation’s second-largest city.

item.title: Live: European stocks plunge after US midterm election results shock markets
item.description: European shares tumbled on Friday as global investors grappled with uncertainty over AI stocks, following the Democrats’ sweeping victory in the US midterm elections. The drop is partly due to fears that Democrats could curb the development of AI data centres, which are widely unpopular among US voters. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

item.title: After cancer surgery, Pope Leo embarks on Latin America trip
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is kicking off a three-nation tour of Latin America with a visit to Uruguay, three weeks after undergoing lung cancer surgery that had put the entire trip into question. (Image credit: Martin Mejia)

item.title: Trump calls midterms 'crooked', demands Alaska votes go to Republican candidate
item.description: Despite having previously accepted the US midterm election results, President Donald Trump told reporters on Thursday the elections were "crooked", and he demanded the remaining votes for Alaska go to its incumbent Republican senator.

item.title: Judge blocks Trump arch hours after federal panel approval
item.description: Ahead of the vote to grant final approval, the Vietnam vet leading a lawsuit to stop the project called it "frankly blasphemous."

item.title: Left-leaning Washington, Colorado join conservative states in banning trans athletes
item.description: Voters in Washington and Colorado have approved measures to ban transgender athletes from participating in school sports

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo brings his international football career to an end
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football on Thursday, ending his 23-year career with Portugal. At 41, the Al-Nassr forward leaves the national team with 234 caps and 146 goals, both world records. As captain, he helped Portugal win Euro 2016 and two Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025. The decision comes after several weeks of tensions with head coach Jorge Jesus, following Ronaldo's departure from the Portugal squad in September.

item.title: South Africa's ANC party on track to face 'nightmare' losses in municipal elections
item.description: South Africa's African National Congress party could face its worst-ever election result on Friday, with early counting suggesting it received only 32% ‌of the vote in the country’s municipal elections. Over two-thirds of votes have been counted so far, and the final results are expected later in the day.

item.title: 'Leaders all over the world understand that Trump is only there for two more years & then he's gone'
item.description: In American politics, even presidential power has its limits. And now, the laws of political gravity may finally be catching up with Donald Trump's hyper-aggressive exercise of executive authority. Following what political scientist Ian Bremmer describes as the most consequential electoral reversal for a governing party in more than half a century, the president and founder of Eurasia Group and GZERO Media argues that the United States has entered a new political phase: the beginning of the end of Trump's ability to dominate the political agenda, at home and on the world stage.

item.title: 4 Colorado officers shot, 1 fatally, after gunfight with suspect: Police
item.description: The suspect was also killed in the gunfire, a police official said.

item.title: Data centers took a beating in the midterm elections
item.description: Opposition to data centers was part of midterm races across the U.S., with campaigns featuring them in hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of TV ads and many winners pledging to clamp down on the energy-hungry behemoths

item.title: A judge blocks construction of Trump's arch moments after it won federal approval
item.description: The Trump administration hoped to begin construction immediately after a federal panel approved its arch late Thursday. But just after midnight, the judge issued an order blocking work for 14 days. (Image credit: Tom Brenner)

item.title: Tech stocks plunge as US midterm results fuel fears of tighter AI rules
item.description: Asian tech stocks fell sharply on Friday, driven by fears of tighter AI regulation following Democrats’ US midterm election victory. US voters widely oppose Data centres, and many winning candidates pledged to curb their development.

item.title: Brand faces 'significant' prison term after rape and sexual assault conviction
item.description: Russell Brand has been told by a judge that he faces a "significant custodial term" after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault.

item.title: WATCH: Authorities reveal motive in Citibank complex shooting
item.description: Chilling surveillance video shows a gunman exchanging gunfire with a security guard after ramming a gate at a Citibank complex near Tampa and killing a woman having lunch, authorities say.

item.title: Rubio denies plans to resign, says working for Trump until end of term has 'always been my plan'
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio dismissed reports on Thursday that he planned to leave the administration after Republican midterm losses, telling The New York Times he intended to serve through the end of President Donald Trump’s term. Rubio, a potential 2028 presidential candidate, declined to discuss his plans.

item.title: Fears of an AI crackdown after midterms spark $2 trillion rout in tech stocks
item.description: Shares sank, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq dropping over 5%, as investors reacted with fear that a Democratic Congress — and states across the country -— would crack down on AI and data centers. (Image credit: Timothy A. Clary)

item.title: Melania Trump touts rare agreement she brokered between Russia and Ukraine
item.description: The six-day pause from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky comes as the administration ramps up efforts to secure an agreement to end the war in Ukraine. (Image credit: Samuel Corum)

item.description: All of these seats were in districts redrawn in 2023 to favor Republican candidates. (Image credit: A.M STEWART/AFP via Getty Images)

item.title: Three-quarters of world's displaced people face severe climate risks, UN says
item.description: Nearly 90 million forcibly displaced people, or three-quarters of the global total, live in countries highly exposed to climate hazards, the UN Refugee Agency said on Friday, urging action ahead of the COP31 climate summit in Turkey. It said droughts, floods and extreme heat were making lasting solutions harder to find.

item.title: WATCH: Jaguars face injury-ravaged Ravens in Thursday Night Football matchup
item.description: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler previews the Jaguars-Ravens matchup, Baltimore’s quarterback injuries and Trevor Lawrence’s strong start to the season.

item.description: ABC News' Rocsi Diaz takes a look at what's buzzing, including Bob Dylan meeting with Pope Leo at the Vatican and Prince William and Prince Harry joining forces to honor their mother.

item.description: The selloff came a day after the Dow soared more than 1,500 points.

item.title: Nigerian court bars opposition candidate two months before election
item.description: In tonight's edition: A Nigerian court disqualifies a leading presidential candidate, adding fresh complications to the electoral process two months before the vote. Also, tens of thousands of people have fled across the border into Kenya as deadly ethnic clashes in southern Ethiopia intensify. Plus having fled conflict and violence, members of the first Refugee Youth Olympic Team are chasing Olympic dreams in Dakar.

item.title: 'Extinction-level event': How Republicans eyeing 2028 are taking midterm losses
item.description: Republicans considering a presidential run offered their assessment of the party's performance in the midterm elections.

item.title: Judge blasts administration for planning to deport Iranians to Iran during wartime
item.description: The Trump administration said during a hearing that it's been making plans to deport Iranian migrants back to Iran during the war, earning a rebuke from a federal judge.

item.title: French protests: 'It's only when public, private sector act together that you can make changes'
item.description: “You can be as repressive as you want. The grievances are still here.” With this stark observation, Ariane Bogain, lecturer in French and politics at Northumbria University, captures the central dilemma confronting the French government: how can political authority be restored when the social and economic grievances driving public anger remain unresolved? Bogain and French politics editor Marc Perelman join Delano D'Souza to examine a protest movement that has evolved beyond its initial demands over purchasing power, fuel prices and education into a broader challenge to the French government. Perelman identifies a striking political paradox: Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon, despite occupying opposing ideological positions, are “objective allies” in their shared electoral interest in weakening the political centre.

item.title: 'Inhumane punishment': Governor Gavin Newsom to commute all 548 California death sentences
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom on Thursday said he would commute all 548 death sentences in the state to life in prison without parole, marking a major step away from capital punishment as he prepares to leave office after eight years.

item.title: Voter frustration about the economy went beyond gas prices, Voter Poll shows
item.description: Three-fours of voters described the economy as not good or poor, polls showed.

item.description: Breakaway men's league LIV Golf is to fold instead of launching a new version because of a lack of financial support.

item.description: The independent third place candidate in Mississippi's tight Senate race, Ty Pinkins, says he did not spoil the race.

item.description: Family, friends and teammates gathered for the funeral of the Spanish footballer who died following an on-field collision with another player.

item.title: France needs 'more public services', 'salaries are too low', 'schools are in very, very bad shape'
item.description: As France confronts another wave of strikes and protests, Gaëlle Martinez, National Secretary of the trade union Solidaires, presents the general strike as more than a confrontation over wages, public spending or the cost of living. Her account reveals a deeper struggle over economic dignity, the future of public services and the democratic right to collective protest. “People just want to live, not survive.” For Martinez, deteriorating schools, insufficient salaries and the dismantling of public services are not isolated policy failures. They are interconnected symptoms of political and economic priorities that, in her assessment, place fiscal restraint above social welfare. Her demand for “a new budget” that is “not based on cuts” is accompanied by a call to “tax the biggest companies, the richest companies where the profits are made.”

item.title: Paraguay's president Pena impeached after resigning over banking scandal
item.description: Paraguay’s lower house voted unanimously to impeach President Santiago Pena on Thursday, just minutes after he announced his resignation on X. Protesters have rallied in the streets since the takeover of a bank linked to Pena blocked millions of people, including pensioners, from accessing their money.

item.title: WATCH: Fuel prices drop after midterm elections
item.description: Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, explains what's behind the decrease in prices.

item.title: Nobel laureate Navi Pillay on fighting violence with justice
item.description: From the International Criminal Court (ICC) to Africa’s place in the global justice system, the stakes are high. In an exclusive interview with FRANCE 24, Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay discusses international justice. She says it must not be held hostage to political power, as US President Donald Trump targets the ICC. What does this showdown mean for Africa?

item.title: US midterms: 'Donald Trump's wings have been more than clipped'
item.description: US President Donald Trump faced a radically transformed and hostile political landscape after Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and the Senate in Tuesday's (November 3) midterms. The result was a personal humiliation for the 80-year-old Trump, leaving him as a lame duck president for the remaining two years of his term. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert has more.
